Individuals are primarily responsible for their safety and property, not the state.
Systemic power structures inherently corrupt individuals and normalize violence when unchecked.
Moral agency is compromised when individuals defer judgment to institutional authority.
Public trust in institutions is eroded when those institutions fail to protect citizens equitably.
Racial injustice in policing reflects deeper structural failures beyond individual bias.
Political polarization stems from a false dichotomy created by the two-party system.
People are capable of moral growth through exposure to truth and empathy, even when indoctrinated by ideology.
Violence, even in self-defense, undermines societal cohesion and increases systemic repression.
